layer1_identification.broadClassification: food prop / stylized low-poly game asset

layer2_form_silhouette.boundingVolume: rounded rectangular box (pan-shaped), near-vertical sides, domed only on top as a RIDGE running the length axis (not a mound peaking at one point - confirmed in loaf-2.png front elevation, where the dome reads as a smooth arch spanning the whole width, and in loaf.png three-quarter, where the ridge crest runs nearly level along most of the length before rounding down at the very ends)
layer2_form_silhouette.symmetry: bilateral both ways (length axis and width axis), broken only by minimal authored jitter

derivedRatios.note: in width=1.0 units: length=1.673, height=1.096 - a squat, elongated pan shape, height only slightly taller than the short-axis width

meso: rounded box corners at both short ends
micro: essentially none - CRIB/GDD instruct minimal detail, smooth is this bread's identity

layer4_spatial: <loaf-dome, above, loaf-body> contact: flush, shared perimeter ring at the crust colour boundary (rimHeightFraction 0.62)

layer5_materials.relief: very low - CRIB explicit instruction: no cracks, no blistering, do not add a displacement grid without dense detail to justify it

layer6_color.observedVsSpec: reference dome reads lighter/more saturated orange under the key light than the flat hex; expected Lambert lighting effect, not a colour bug (same pattern documented in pancake/scone material-pass notes)

layer7_identity_features: angular near-vertical sides with only a small corner/foot bevel - if the sides go fully round it reads as a generic round loaf, losing the 'pan-baked' identity (loaf.json notes_ko)
dome confined strictly to the top face, never bleeding onto the side walls
ridge dome (arch along the length), not a mound (peak at one point) - confirmed by the front elevation's smooth level-topped arch and the top-down view's fairly flat/even shading band down the centre
layer8_uncertainty: underside never visible in any view; modelled as a closed flat cap

exact taper profile at the very ends is inferred from the three-quarter view's visible corner rounding, not independently measured - treated as an approximate corner bevel, matching how pancake/scone treated their own unmeasured corner curvature
